newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to raise Danish gas oil output.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to raise Danish gas oil output.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it planned to upgrade conversion capacity at the Kalundborg refinery in Denmark to boost output of gas oil by around 175,000 tonnes per year.

Kalundborg has a crude throughput capacity of five million tonnes a year of which gas oil output accounts for 35 percent, jet fuel 10 percent, gasoline 27 percent, liquefied petroleum gases (LPG) five percent and heavy fuel oil 23 percent.
John Berg, production vice president at the refinery, said the company would reduce production of heavy fuel oil and raise gas oil output.
"We are seeing a decrease in the market for heavy fuel oil. The extra gas oil will mainly go to the export market," Berg told Reuters.
Work on Kalundborg, which is situated close to the Danish capital Copenhagen, will begin in the autumn and is scheduled to be completed early in 1999.
